indicators.note: a flier who crashes ends up wrecked, so the letters of the word are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: An aviator comes down at the cathedral city of Winchester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashes' rearranges FLIER. Winchester looks like the English city but is the make of gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Winchester is a famous American make of repeating firearm, a shoulder gun.

definitions.meaning: a senior churchman who heads a diocese
a chess piece that moves diagonally across the board

explanation.definitionFit: A senior cleric of the church is also the name of the diagonal-moving chess piece.

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level

indicators.note: churning stirs things vigorously, so the letters of the next word are mixed up

explanation.surface: A dairy's usual way of churning milk into cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to churn' is the anagram signal on 'means'; churning suggests butter-making, a dairy red herring before the cheese arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard Italian grating cheese from the Parma region.

clue.text: Set old boy back with sham remedy

parts.note: to set something down is to place it

indicators.note: the abbreviation for the former pupil is read backwards

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil of a school

explanation.surface: A former pupil is put back on his feet with a fake cure.
explanation.walkthrough: OB, for a former pupil of a school, is a British convention; 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy pill given with no active medicine, working only through the patient's belief.

parts.note: going means departing or leaving
a son can mean a follower or disciple, as in 'sons of the prophets'

explanation.surface: A follower, on departing, exposes shady goings-on.
explanation.definitionFit: Shady or questionable activities or behaviour.

clue.text: Device to secure any pets, if loose

explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' rearranges ANY PETS IF; in the surface 'if' reads as 'in case', but it is part of the fodder.

clue.text: To understand, I score with the fingers

parts.note: to dig is slang for to understand or appreciate
a tally is a score or count

explanation.surface: Counting up to understand, using one's fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: Digits are fingers, so doing something by hand is doing it with digits.

parts.note: a citizen of Italy's capital city, and also the upright typeface, as opposed to italic

explanation.surface: A question about what kind of capital letter to use.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Rome is a citizen of a capital, and the plain upright printing font shares the name.

clue.text: Lincoln left as first murder victim

parts.note: Abe is the short name of Abraham Lincoln, the US president

explanation.surface: President Lincoln was left as the first victim of an assassination.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Adam's son killed by his brother Cain is the Bible's first murder victim.

clue.text: Michael C. Strange describing work on transmutation

explanation.surface: A man named Michael C. Strange writes about turning lead into gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' looks like a surname, but it rearranges MICHAEL C.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval pseudo-science that sought to turn base metals into gold; the adjective describes such work.

clue.text: Old car can produce black rage

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
anger is rage

explanation.surface: A clapped-out vehicle drives its owner to fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a dilapidated, noisy old motor vehicle.

definitions.meaning: Lord Greystoke is Tarzan, who was raised in the jungle by great primates

definitions.meaning: the burglar Bill Sikes in Dickens's Oliver Twist owns a dog of this name
a dart or arrow hitting the dead centre of a target

explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's villain owns a dog with this name, and a perfect hit on a target's centre has the same name.

clue.text: Border in slight depression, going different ways

parts.note: a dint is a small dent or hollow
a verge is a border or edge

explanation.definitionFit: Paths that separate and head off in other directions.

clue.text: Mine, carrying £25, was kept in the stalls

indicators.note: the mine word comes first and carries the money word along after it

pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds

explanation.definitionFit: A small horse that hauled coal underground and was stabled below ground in stalls.

parts.note: oat breakfast food, but also British slang for a prison sentence, served in 'jugs', slang for jails

parts.note: an antic is a playful caper or prank

explanation.definitionFit: Wildly hurried and agitated, like a hectic scramble.

indicators.note: being sacked throws things into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fashion designer who has been fired accepts it without complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Accepting a situation meekly without objection.

definitions.meaning: a university in the English county town of Berkshire
a performer's rendering of a piece of music

explanation.definitionFit: The Berkshire town has a university, and a musician's interpretation of a score is the same word.

definitions.note: describes the thing carried on the bike rather than naming it

parts.note: gear means clothes or kit
a case is a bag

explanation.surface: A luggage bag strapped on a cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the item ('one carried on a bicycle'): a cover around a bike's chain and gears.
explanation.definitionFit: A protective guard enclosing the chain and sprockets, fitted to a bike frame.

parts.note: LMS was the London, Midland and Scottish Railway, an old British rail line

explanation.surface: Help provided for a disused railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: Charity given to the poor as relief.

indicators.note: the word reads the same forwards and backwards, in both directions

explanation.surface: Someone checks left and right before crossing.

indicators.note: turning the letters round puts them in a different order

explanation.surface: An exhibition tours the city of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: To display or reveal a feeling or quality.

indicators.note: damaged fruit is spoiled, and the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A bruised peach is sold for very little.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexpensive, at a low price.

clue.text: Go semi-mad looking after number one?

indicators.note: going mad scrambles the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Becoming half crazy from caring only about yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-centredness, putting yourself first above others.

to box is to fight

explanation.definitionFit: Close-range combat between fighter planes.

clue.text: Problems for inferior horses after opening of Sandown

indicators.note: the horses come after the first letter of the racecourse
the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: nags are poor, worn-out horses

explanation.surface: Trouble for second-rate horses after the start at Sandown racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandown Park is a British racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Snags are hitches or difficulties.

clue.text: Primer hidden here on the person

definitions.meaning: a first coat of paint applied before the top coat
something concealed beneath the outer garment someone wears
